What we are testing: Sign in with email and password
Before you start: You have an account and its password.
What to do:
1. Open the portal.
2. Enter your email and password.
3. Press Sign in.
What you should see: The password step is accepted and the screen asks for a code.

What we are testing: The code arrives and signs you in
Before you start: You are on the code step from T-01.
What to do:
1. Read the code that was sent to you.
2. Enter it.
3. Press Verify.
What you should see: You land on the dashboard, signed in, with your name shown.

Before you start: You are on the code step.
What to do:
1. Enter a code that is not the one you were sent.
2. Press Verify.
What you should see: You are told the code is wrong and you stay signed out.

What we are testing: A code cannot be used twice
Before you start: You have signed in once with a code (T-02).
What to do:
1. Sign out.
2. Sign in again with the same email and password.
3. Enter the PREVIOUS code.
What you should see: The old code is refused; only the new one works.

Before you start: You know the account's real password.
What to do:
1. Enter the right email with a wrong password.
2. Press Sign in.
What you should see: You are told the details are wrong. No code is sent.

Before you start: You can read the mail for this account.
What to do:
1. Press Forgot password.
2. Enter your email.
3. Follow the mail and set a new password.
4. Sign in with the new password.
What you should see: The new password works and the old one no longer does.

What to do:
1. Reload the page.
2. Open another screen.
What you should see: You stay signed in; you are not asked for the code again.

What to do:
1. Press Sign out.
2. Press the browser Back button.
What you should see: You are returned to the sign-in screen and Back does not get you in.

What to do:
1. Open the account details.
2. Change a contact detail and save.
3. Reload the page.
What you should see: The change is saved and shown after reloading.
Notes: See known issues — this currently fails.

What to do:
1. Press Create New.
2. Fill in a name, an email and permissions.
3. Save.
4. Sign in as that account in another browser profile.
What you should see: The account appears in the list and can sign in.

Before you start: The account from T-10, with only Calls allowed.
What to do:
1. Edit its permissions to Calls only.
2. Sign in as that account.
What you should see: Only the screens it is allowed appear; the rest are not reachable, including by typing the address.

Before you start: An account with read-only rights on a screen.
What to do:
1. Sign in as it.
2. Open that screen and try to save a change.
What you should see: The screen opens, the save is refused, nothing changes.

What to do:
1. Open it.
2. Press Reset Password.
3. Sign in with the new password.
What you should see: The new password works; the old one does not.

What to do:
1. Open an account.
2. Press Generate Basic Auth Token.
3. Note it.
What you should see: A token is shown and can be copied.

What to do:
1. Switch it off.
2. Try to sign in as it.
What you should see: It cannot sign in while disabled, and can again once re-enabled.

What to do:
1. Delete it.
2. Reload the list.
3. Try to sign in as it.
What you should see: It is gone from the list and cannot sign in.

Before you start: needs: a second customer on the same system.
What to do:
1. Sign in as an account of customer A.
2. Open the accounts list.
What you should see: Only customer A's accounts are listed. Nothing of customer B appears anywhere.

Before you start: More than a page of accounts.
What to do:
1. Search for one by name or email.
2. Page through the list.
What you should see: The search finds it and paging does not lose or repeat rows.

What to do:
1. Open your account.
2. Change your display name and save.
3. Reload.
What you should see: The new name is kept and is shown in the top bar.

What to do:
1. Open the customer details.
2. Change the company contact details and save.
3. Reload.
What you should see: The change is kept.

Before you start: needs: an account with more than one customer.
What to do:
1. Use the customer switcher.
2. Open Devices and Calls.
What you should see: Every screen now shows the other customer's data, and nothing of the first.

What to do:
1. Change your password.
2. Sign out and back in.
What you should see: Only the new password works.

What to do:
1. Create an application with a name and a domain.
2. Save.
What you should see: It appears in the list and can be picked in the environment selector.

What to do:
1. Change its name and save.
2. Reload.
What you should see: The new name shows everywhere it is listed.

What we are testing: Give an account access to it
Before you start: The application from T-23 and a second account.
What to do:
1. Add the application to that account.
2. Sign in as that account.
What you should see: The account can now pick that application and see its data.

Before you start: An application with at least one device, one user and one number on it.
What to do:
1. Note what is on it.
2. Delete it.
3. Open Devices, Users and Routing.
What you should see: The application is gone AND everything that belonged to it is gone too — no leftover devices, users or numbers.
Notes: The point of this row is the leftovers, not the application.

What to do:
1. Select more than one.
2. Apply a change to all of them.
What you should see: Every selected application is changed; the others are untouched.

What to do:
1. Press Create User.
2. Fill in name, email and extension number.
3. Save.
4. Open Devices.
What you should see: The user is listed AND a device for them appears on Devices.

What we are testing: The new user's phone can register
Before you start: The user from T-28. needs: a softphone.
What to do:
1. Configure the softphone with that extension and its password.
2. Register it.
3. Open Devices.
What you should see: The phone registers and the device shows as online.
Notes: A device that exists but was never sent to its node looks fine here and refuses every registration — this row is what catches that.

What we are testing: The user can sign in to the portal
What to do: 1. Sign in at the user portal with their email and password.
What you should see: They reach their own screens (My calls, Phone) and see only their own calls.

What to do:
1. Change their name and save.
2. Reload.
What you should see: The change is kept and shows on their device too.

Before you start: A CSV of a few users.
What to do:
1. Press Import CSV.
2. Choose the file.
3. Import.
What you should see: Every row in the file becomes a user, and the count matches. Bad rows are reported rather than silently skipped.

What to do:
1. Delete them.
2. Open Devices.
3. Try to register their softphone.
What you should see: The user and their device are gone and the phone can no longer register.

What to do:
1. Press Add Device.
2. Fill in Name, Device Number and SIP Password.
3. Save.
What you should see: It appears in the list straight away.

Before you start: The device from T-34. needs: a softphone.
What to do:
1. Point the softphone at the platform with that number and password.
2. Register.
3. Reload the list.
What you should see: The device shows as registered / online.

Before you start: Two registered devices. needs: two softphones.
What to do: 1. From device A, dial device B's number.
What you should see: B rings, the call connects, both sides have audio, and hanging up ends it on both.

What to do:
1. Set the wrong SIP password on the softphone.
2. Register.
What you should see: Registration is refused and the device stays offline.

What to do:
1. Change its name and save.
2. Reload.
What you should see: The change is kept.

What to do:
1. Change its SIP password.
2. Re-register the softphone with the new one.
What you should see: The new password works; the old one is refused.

Before you start: A CSV of a few devices.
What to do:
1. Press Import CSV.
2. Choose the file and import.
What you should see: Every row becomes a device and the count matches.

Before you start: More than a page of devices.
What to do:
1. Use the filters and the search box.
2. Page through.
What you should see: Results match what you asked for; paging does not lose or repeat rows.

What to do:
1. Delete it.
2. Try to register its softphone.
What you should see: It is gone from the list and can no longer register.

What to do:
1. Press Add DID.
2. Enter the number and save.
What you should see: It is listed against that application.

Before you start: The number from T-43 and a registered device. needs: a way to dial the number.
What to do:
1. Point the number at that device.
2. Call the number from outside.
What you should see: The device rings, the call connects with audio both ways.

What we are testing: A number goes to an IVR
Before you start: An IVR with at least one option.
What to do:
1. Point the number at the IVR.
2. Call it.
3. Press the option.
What you should see: You hear the menu and the key press takes you where the option says.

What we are testing: A number goes to a queue
Before you start: A queue with an agent logged in.
What to do:
1. Point the number at the queue.
2. Call it.
What you should see: You hear the queue treatment and the agent's phone rings.

Before you start: A call condition for out of hours.
What to do:
1. Put a condition on the number so out of hours goes elsewhere.
2. Call it inside hours, then outside.
What you should see: Each call lands where the condition says.

Before you start: A number that is fully set up.
What to do:
1. Press Duplicate DID.
2. Give it another number and save.
What you should see: The copy has the same routing, with the new number.

What to do: 1. Import DIDs from CSV.
What you should see: Every row becomes a number and the count matches.

What to do:
1. Delete it.
2. Call it.
What you should see: It is gone from the list and the call is not answered by the platform.

Before you start: needs: two PBXs / sites connected by a trunk rule.
What to do: 1. From a phone on site A, dial a site B extension.
What you should see: The call reaches site B and connects.

What you should see: The device rings, the call connects, and it appears in the live list while it runs.

What you should see: Both phones drop within a second or two and the call leaves the live list.

What to do:
1. Open it in the call log.
2. Play the recording.
What you should see: It plays, and it is the right call.

What to do: 1. Use spy / listen on that call.

What you should see: The ringing call is answered on your device and stops ringing on the first.

What to do:

What to do: 1. Send a message to the platform number from outside.
What you should see: It appears in Messages against the right conversation.

What you should see: No further numbers are dialled.

Before you start: needs: a URL you can watch (any request-catching site).
What to do:

2. Choose webhook, paste the URL, pick when it should fire and which applications it covers.
3. Save.
What you should see: It is listed as enabled.

What to do:

What to do:

2. Make a call on B, then on A.
What you should see: Only the call on A is sent.

What to do:

Block: THE WHOLE WAY THROUGH — run this last
What we are testing: A new customer, end to end
Before you start: You are signed in with full access. needs: two softphones and a number.
What to do:
1. Create an application.
2. Create two users on it.
3. Register both softphones.
4. Add a number and point it at one of them.
5. Call between the two devices.
6. Call the number from outside.
7. Open the call log, the dashboard and Transactions.
What you should see: Every step works without a developer touching anything, and the calls you made are the calls the log, the dashboard and the charges show.
Notes: If this row passes, the release is usable. If it fails, the release is not, whatever else passed.
